UNDERSTANDING YOUR STATEMENT
Last reviewed: 02 September 2026 · Reading time: 4 minutes

Your statement shows every payment into and out of your account during the statement period, with
the balance after each day's transactions. Here's what each part means.

1. Your account details
Your sort code is a six-digit number written as three pairs (for example 00-00-00) and your account
number has eight digits. Together they identify your account for payments within the UK. For
payments from abroad you'll need your IBAN (22 characters for UK accounts, starting GB) and our BIC,
TBNKGB2E. You'll find all of these at the top of page 1 and in the app under Account > Details.

2. Transaction codes
Each line starts with a short code that tells you how the money moved:

  Code   Meaning                                  Example description
  BGC    Bank Giro Credit (e.g. salary, benefits) BGC [EMPLOYER NAME] SALARY
  FPI    Faster Payment received                  FPI [PAYER NAME] [THEIR REFERENCE]
  FPO    Faster Payment sent                      FPO [PAYEE NAME] [YOUR REFERENCE]
  SO     Standing order                           SO [PAYEE NAME] [REFERENCE]
  DD     Direct Debit                             DD [COMPANY] [YOUR CUSTOMER REF]
  CHQ    Cheque paid out                          CHQ 000123
  ATM    Cash machine withdrawal                  ATM [LOCATION] [DATE]
  POS    Card payment in a shop or online         POS [MERCHANT] [TOWN] CD [LAST 4 DIGITS]
  INT    Interest paid to you                     INT GROSS
  FEE    Account fee                              FEE MONTHLY PREMIER

Card payments show the last four digits of the card used, so you can tell which card a payment was
made with if you have more than one. We never print your full card number on a statement.

3. Direct Debits
The Direct Debit Guarantee protects you if a company takes the wrong amount or takes a payment on
the wrong date. Each company that collects Direct Debits has a six-digit Service User Number (SUN),
for example British Gas 942871 or Thames Water 991216. The reference shown is the one the company
uses for your account with them. Payments under the European SEPA scheme show a Creditor Identifier
instead, such as DE98ZZZ09999999999, and a mandate reference.

4. Paying HMRC
If you pay Self Assessment tax by bank transfer, use HMRC's account (sort code 08-32-10, account
12001039) and quote your 10-digit Unique Taxpayer Reference followed by the letter K. Never send
your UTR to anyone who contacts you unexpectedly.

5. Fees and charges (Classic Current account)
  Arranged overdraft                          39.9% EAR variable
  Unarranged overdraft                        not available - payments will be returned
  Non-sterling transaction fee                2.75% of the transaction value
  Cash withdrawals abroad                     £1.50 per withdrawal
  Copy statement (per sheet)                  £5.00
  CHAPS payment (branch)                      £25.00

6. Spotted something you don't recognise?
Check whether the merchant name is different from the shop's trading name - for example a card
payment at a café inside a museum may show the operator's name, and online marketplaces often show
"AMZNMKTPLACE" or "PAYPAL *" followed by the seller. If you still don't recognise it, freeze your card
in the app and call us on 0345 600 2290 (from abroad +44 131 496 0000). We will never ask you to move
money to a "safe account".
